faqs.q: What is a Destaco 030 series hydraulic swing/pull clamp used for?
faqs.a: The Destaco 030 series is a hydraulic swing/pull clamp: the arm swings clear of the workpiece, then pulls it down on to the fixture. The maker states 5,000 psi (345 bar), and the series is listed in 24 part numbers, single- or double-acting, with right- or left-hand swing; see the [swing clamps shelf](/c/hydraulic-swing-clamps).

faqs.q: How do I read a Destaco 030 part number such as 030-1-D-4000-R?
faqs.a: In the rows, 030-1 is the series, S or D matches the single-acting or double-acting description, the number (475, 1100, 2400, 4000) is the size, and an R or L ending matches right-hand or left-hand swing. For example 030-1-D-475-R is listed as a double-acting right-hand swing clamp, and 030-1-S-1100-L as a single-acting 22.6 mm stroke left-hand clamp.

faqs.q: What strokes do the Destaco 030 swing/pull clamps have?
faqs.a: The rows give strokes of 0.65 in (16.5 mm) for the 475 size, 0.89 in (22.6 mm) for the 1100, 1.07 in (27.2 mm) for the 4000 and 1.12 in (28.4 mm) for the 2400. Choose the stroke for the full travel your fixture needs.

faqs.q: Single-acting or double-acting: which Destaco 030 clamp do I need?
faqs.a: Single-acting (S) clamps are listed alongside double-acting (D) versions in every size. Choose double-acting where the arm must be driven back by oil, and single-acting where a return spring or the circuit design is acceptable.

faqs.q: What pressure is the Destaco 030 series swing/pull clamp rated for?
faqs.a: The maker states 5,000 psi (345 bar) for the Destaco 030 series, and the size table repeats 5,000 psi on the rows that give a rating. High-pressure tooling cylinders need a matching pump, hose and gauge rated for that pressure.

faqs.q: Which swing directions does the Destaco 030 series come in?
faqs.a: Both are listed: right-hand swing (R) and left-hand swing (L), for example 030-1-S-475-R and 030-1-S-475-L. Rotation is chosen on the part number, so check the direction on your fixture before ordering.

faqs.q: What body does the Destaco 030 series have, and what does it connect to?
faqs.a: Several rows are described as threaded-body swing cylinders, so they screw into a fixture bore and take oil through a port in the fixture. Check the thread and port on the part number you order, and use hose and fittings rated for 5,000 psi.

faqs.q: How do I size a Destaco 030 swing/pull clamp for a fixture?
faqs.a: Choose capacity with margin over the working load and stroke for the full travel needed, as the listing advises. The series covers the 475, 1100, 2400 and 4000 sizes in the part numbers.

faqs.q: Which other swing clamps does Indus list besides the Destaco 030?
faqs.a: The [Enerpac SC swing clamps](/p/enerpac-sc-swing-clamps) are cartridge swing clamps in 14 models from 475 to 2600 lbs force, and the [Enerpac swing clamp cylinders](/p/enerpac-swing-clamp-cylinders) go up to 7600 lbs. Compare force, stroke and mounting before choosing.

faqs.q: How does the Destaco 030 compare with the Destaco 10 series threaded body cylinders?
faqs.a: The 030 is a swing/pull clamp with an arm that swings clear then clamps, rated 5,000 psi (345 bar), while the [Destaco 10 series](/p/destaco-10-series-threaded-body-cylinders) are threaded-body cylinders rated 3,000 psi (207 bar). Use the 030 when the arm must swing away to load the part.

faqs.q: Where is the Destaco 030 series made?
faqs.a: The listing gives Taiwan as the country of origin. We ship it from Dubai, UAE to the GCC, Africa and beyond; tell us the destination so the paperwork matches.

faqs.a: Yes. In Dubai, UAE we stock Destaco 030 series swing/pull clamps and ship worldwide with the best lead times. Tell us sizes and quantities on [our contact page](/contact) and we will quote.

faqs.q: What is a Destaco 10 series threaded body cylinder used for?
faqs.a: The Destaco 10 series is a hydraulic threaded-body cylinder that screws into a fixture and pushes with a pressure point for clamping or positioning. The maker states 3,000 psi (207 bar), and the range has 7 part numbers on the [swing clamps shelf](/c/hydraulic-swing-clamps).

faqs.q: What do the Destaco 010 part numbers mean?
faqs.a: The part numbers are 010-210-400, 010-210-501, 010-211-002, 010-211-004, 010-211-502, 010-211-504 and 010-212-004. The descriptions give the bore or thread of the body (3/8 in bore, 1-1/2 in bore, 3/4-16, 2 1/2 16) and the stroke, so match the thread and stroke to your fixture bore.

faqs.q: What strokes do the Destaco 10 series cylinders have?
faqs.a: The rows give strokes of 0.22, 0.31, 0.5 and 1 in. The shortest is the 3/8 in bore 010-210-400 at 0.22 in, and the longest are 010-211-004 and 010-212-004 at 1 in.

faqs.q: What threads do the Destaco 10 series threaded bodies have?
faqs.a: The descriptions show 3/4-16 on 010-210-501, 2 1/2 16 on 010-212-004 and 1-1/2 in bore on 010-211-504. Check the thread on the row before drilling your fixture.

faqs.q: What pressure is the Destaco 10 series rated for?
faqs.a: The maker states 3,000 psi (207 bar), and the rows that give a rating show 3,000 psi. Use hose, fittings and a gauge rated for at least that pressure.

faqs.q: Are the Destaco 10 series cylinders single or double acting?
faqs.a: The descriptions say single-acting for the pressure-point rows, so they extend on oil pressure and return by spring. The rows without a note should be confirmed against the part number before ordering.

faqs.q: What do I need to fit with the Destaco 10 series cylinder?
faqs.a: You need a fixture bore with the matching thread, a hydraulic supply at no more than 3,000 psi, and a manifold or drilled port. [Contact us](/contact) with the part number and we confirm the thread and port.

faqs.q: How do I install a Destaco 10 series threaded body cylinder?
faqs.a: Screw the body into the tapped fixture bore, connect the oil port and bleed the line before clamping. Choose capacity with margin over the working load and stroke for the travel you need.

faqs.q: Where are threaded body cylinders used?
faqs.a: They are used in clamping fixtures where a compact screw-in cylinder pushes a pressure point, such as workholding and positioning. The [721E screw-in cylinders](/p/destaco-721e-series-hydraulic-screw-in-cylinders) are a related screw-in range.

faqs.q: How does the Destaco 10 series compare with the 722D block cylinders?
faqs.a: The 10 series is a threaded-body cylinder rated 3,000 psi (207 bar), while the [722D series block cylinders](/p/destaco-722d-series-double-acting-hydraulic-block-cylinders) are double-acting at 7,250 psi (500 bar). Choose the 722D where the higher pressure is needed.

faqs.q: What is a Destaco 721D series short stroke double-acting cylinder used for?
faqs.a: The Destaco 721D series is a double-acting hydraulic hollow-piston cylinder for clamping, listed with 4 part numbers and a maker rating of 5,000 psi (345 bar). Hydraulic oil drives it both ways, which suits fixtures that need positive release; browse the [swing clamps shelf](/c/hydraulic-swing-clamps).

faqs.q: What are the Destaco 721D part numbers?
faqs.a: The rows are 721D25501-2, 725D35151-2, 725D63171-1 and 725D80151-1. The descriptions give the type as a double-action hollow piston cylinder with the stroke, so quote the part number from your fixture drawing.

faqs.q: What strokes do the Destaco 721D cylinders have?
faqs.a: The size table gives strokes of 0.59 in on three rows and 0.67 in on one. These are short-stroke cylinders, so check that the stroke covers your clamping travel.

faqs.q: What does hollow piston mean on a Destaco 721D cylinder?
faqs.a: The descriptions call these hollow-piston double-action cylinders, meaning the piston is hollow. The listing shows no spindle included, so any spindle or tool is bought separately.

faqs.q: Does Indus provide test documents with the Destaco 721D?
faqs.a: No certificate or approval is listed for these cylinders. If your project needs a test report, state it on your [request](/contact) and we confirm what is available.

faqs.q: Does the Destaco 721D come with a spindle?
faqs.a: No, the specification says Spindle Included: No. The cylinder is listed for clamping applications, so add the clamping spindle or pad that your fixture needs.

faqs.q: How do I size a Destaco 721D cylinder?
faqs.a: Choose capacity with margin over the working load and stroke for the full travel, as the listing advises. The stroke on the four rows is 0.59 or 0.67 in.

faqs.q: Where are the Destaco 721D short stroke cylinders used?
faqs.a: The Destaco 721D short stroke cylinders are used in machining fixtures and workholding where a hydraulic clamp or support must hold the part during cutting. See other clamp types on the [swing clamps shelf](/c/hydraulic-swing-clamps).

faqs.q: How does the Destaco 721D differ from the 721E screw-in cylinder?
faqs.a: The 721D is double acting at 5,000 psi (345 bar) with a 0.59 to 0.67 in stroke; the [721E](/p/destaco-721e-series-hydraulic-screw-in-cylinders) is single acting with stroke from 0.39 to 1.97 in and ratings from 2,625 to 5,075 psi.

faqs.q: What is a Destaco 721E series screw-in cylinder used for?
faqs.a: The Destaco 721E series is a single-acting hydraulic screw-in cylinder that threads into a fixture to push or clamp. It is listed in 24 part numbers with ratings from 2,625 to 5,075 psi (181 to 350 bar) by size; see the [swing clamps shelf](/c/hydraulic-swing-clamps).

faqs.q: How do I read a Destaco 721E part number such as 721E16121-2?
faqs.a: The numbers start 721E followed by a size code, for example 721E08101-2, 721E12101-2, 721E16121-2 and 721E20161-2. The descriptions give the stroke in mm, so match the stroke on the row to your fixture.
